question.text: What does a driver license require of your health?

answer.text: Both physical and mental health shape how you drive, and a driver license requires that you be in good health.

teaching.text: Physical and mental health both shape your driving, and a license assumes good health. Remember: good health to drive.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Both physical and mental health shape how you drive, and a driver license requires that you be in good health.

question.text: How can a cold, a headache or the flu affect your driving?

answer.text: Even a short illness such as a cold, a headache or the flu can leave you less alert and slower to respond behind the wheel.

teaching.text: A cold, a headache or the flu can make you less alert and slower to react. Remember: sick means slower.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Even a short illness such as a cold, a headache or the flu can leave you less alert and slower to respond behind the wheel.

question.text: Why is even a brief nod-off at highway speed so dangerous?

answer.text: At fifty-five miles per hour a vehicle covers the length of a football field in three point seven seconds, so even a brief nod-off is dangerous.

teaching.text: At fifty-five miles per hour, a car crosses a football field in under four seconds, so a short nod-off is dangerous. Remember: a nod covers a field.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At fifty-five miles per hour a vehicle covers the length of a football field in three point seven seconds, so even a brief nod-off is dangerous.

question.text: Where and when do drowsy-driving crashes happen most often?

answer.text: Crashes caused by drowsiness tend to be serious and happen most often on fast rural highways when the driver is traveling alone.

teaching.text: Drowsy crashes tend to be serious and are most common on fast rural highways with a lone driver. Remember: fast rural roads, alone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Crashes caused by drowsiness tend to be serious and happen most often on fast rural highways when the driver is traveling alone.

question.text: What are the warning signs that you are getting drowsy behind the wheel?

answer.text: Signs of drowsiness include not remembering the last few miles, hitting a rumble strip or drifting out of your lane, yawning again and again, and struggling to focus or keep your eyes open.

teaching.text: Lost miles, rumble strips, lane drifting, repeated yawning and heavy eyes all signal drowsiness. Remember: yawns, drifting, lost miles.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Signs of drowsiness include not remembering the last few miles, hitting a rumble strip or drifting out of your lane, yawning again and again, and struggling to focus or keep your eyes open.

question.text: What should you do if you grow tired while driving, and how long do quick fixes help?

answer.text: If you grow tired while driving you should stop; a nap of fifteen to forty-five minutes and some caffeine help only for a while.

teaching.text: When tired, stop; a fifteen to forty-five minute nap and caffeine only help for a while. Remember: tired means stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you grow tired while driving you should stop; a nap of fifteen to forty-five minutes and some caffeine help only for a while.

question.text: How often should you take a break on a long drive, and what should you do?

answer.text: On a long drive, take a break at least every two hours: leave the car, stretch and walk briskly.

teaching.text: On long drives, stop at least every two hours to get out, stretch and walk briskly. Remember: break every two hours.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a long drive, take a break at least every two hours: leave the car, stretch and walk briskly.

question.text: What daily driving limit and medicine advice does the handbook give?

answer.text: The handbook suggests capping your driving at about three hundred to four hundred miles a day and avoiding medicines that make you drowsy.

teaching.text: Keep daily driving to about three hundred to four hundred miles and avoid medicines that cause drowsiness. Remember: limit miles, skip drowsy pills.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The handbook suggests capping your driving at about three hundred to four hundred miles a day and avoiding medicines that make you drowsy.

question.text: How is a nap with caffeine different from the regular long-trip break?

answer.text: A short nap with caffeine is only a temporary help for fatigue, while the long-trip habit is a stop at least every two hours.

teaching.text: A nap and caffeine are a short bridge, while a break every two hours is the routine habit. Remember: naps help briefly, breaks regularly.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A short nap with caffeine is only a temporary help for fatigue, while the long-trip habit is a stop at least every two hours.

question.text: What is distracted driving?

answer.text: Distracted driving means any activity that might pull your attention away from the main job of driving.

teaching.text: Any activity that might pull your attention away from driving is a distraction. Remember: anything off the main job.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Distracted driving means any activity that might pull your attention away from the main job of driving.

question.text: What are some common distractions behind the wheel?

answer.text: Common distractions include texting, phone use, eating or drinking, talking with passengers, grooming, reading maps, using navigation, watching video and adjusting audio equipment.

teaching.text: Phones, food and drink, passengers, grooming, maps, navigation, video and audio controls are all common distractions. Remember: phones, food, talk, maps.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Common distractions include texting, phone use, eating or drinking, talking with passengers, grooming, reading maps, using navigation, watching video and adjusting audio equipment.

question.text: How does distraction change a driver's reactions and awareness?

answer.text: Distracted drivers respond more slowly to events such as a car slowing to turn or pulling out of a side road, and they miss hazards like pedestrians or debris more often.

teaching.text: Distracted drivers react more slowly and miss pedestrians and debris more often. Remember: distracted means late.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Distracted drivers respond more slowly to events such as a car slowing to turn or pulling out of a side road, and they miss hazards like pedestrians or debris more often.

question.text: Why do many distractions make it harder to avoid a crash?

answer.text: Many distractions make it harder to steer clear of a crash because they take at least one hand off the steering wheel.

teaching.text: Many distractions take a hand off the wheel, making a crash harder to avoid. Remember: both hands on the wheel.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Many distractions make it harder to steer clear of a crash because they take at least one hand off the steering wheel.

question.text: When does the handbook say a phone may be used while driving?

answer.text: Use a phone while driving only when truly necessary, for emergencies or to reach a parent, legal guardian or spouse, and only at a safe time and place.

teaching.text: Use the phone only when truly necessary, for emergencies or family, at a safe time and place. Remember: only when truly necessary.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Use a phone while driving only when truly necessary, for emergencies or to reach a parent, legal guardian or spouse, and only at a safe time and place.

question.text: What phone habits does the handbook recommend for drivers?

answer.text: Let a passenger make the call for you, let unanswered calls go to a message, and secure the phone so it cannot fly around in a crash.

teaching.text: Let a passenger make calls, let calls go to a message, and secure the phone so it cannot fly around. Remember: let it ring, secure it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Let a passenger make the call for you, let unanswered calls go to a message, and secure the phone so it cannot fly around in a crash.

question.text: What phone activity is unlawful for every North Carolina driver?

answer.text: North Carolina makes it unlawful to text or email on a cell phone while driving on a public street, highway or public vehicular area.

teaching.text: Every driver is barred from texting or email while driving on public roads and vehicular areas. Remember: no texting while driving.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: North Carolina makes it unlawful to text or email on a cell phone while driving on a public street, highway or public vehicular area.

question.text: What phone use is allowed for a driver under eighteen while the vehicle is moving?

answer.text: A driver under eighteen may not use a cell phone or related technology at all while the vehicle is moving, except to call nine one one in an emergency.

teaching.text: Under eighteen, no phone or related technology while moving, except an emergency call to nine one one. Remember: under eighteen, no phone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver under eighteen may not use a cell phone or related technology at all while the vehicle is moving, except to call nine one one in an emergency.

question.text: How does the phone law for all drivers differ from the law for drivers under eighteen?

answer.text: Every driver is barred from texting or emailing while driving, but a driver under eighteen is barred from using a phone at all while moving, apart from a nine one one emergency call.

teaching.text: Every driver is barred from texting, but drivers under eighteen are barred from any phone use while moving. Remember: all no texts, teens none.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every driver is barred from texting or emailing while driving, but a driver under eighteen is barred from using a phone at all while moving, apart from a nine one one emergency call.

question.text: What phone use is allowed while driving a school bus?

answer.text: No one may drive a school bus on a public road or vehicular area while using a cell phone or other mobile-device technology.

teaching.text: Nobody may drive a school bus while using a cell phone or mobile-device technology. Remember: no phone on the bus.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: No one may drive a school bus on a public road or vehicular area while using a cell phone or other mobile-device technology.

question.text: Which phone rules are laws, and which are safety advice?

answer.text: The texting ban and the under-eighteen ban are laws, while advice to use a phone only for emergencies or family contact is a safety reminder rather than a separate legal rule.

teaching.text: The texting and under-eighteen bans are laws, while using the phone only when necessary is safety advice. Remember: laws versus good advice.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The texting ban and the under-eighteen ban are laws, while advice to use a phone only for emergencies or family contact is a safety reminder rather than a separate legal rule.

question.text: How should you handle a medicine that may affect your driving?

answer.text: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect driving, so learn how a medicine affects you and drive as little as possible while taking it.

teaching.text: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can both affect driving, so learn their effects and drive less while taking them. Remember: know your medicine.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect driving, so learn how a medicine affects you and drive as little as possible while taking it.

question.text: About what share of traffic deaths involve alcohol, according to the handbook?

answer.text: The handbook states that about thirty-eight percent of all traffic deaths involve alcohol.

teaching.text: The handbook says about thirty-eight percent of traffic deaths involve alcohol. Remember: alcohol in many deaths.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The handbook states that about thirty-eight percent of all traffic deaths involve alcohol.

question.text: What kind of drug is alcohol, and what does it do to your reactions?

answer.text: Alcohol is a depressant that slows the brain, so you cannot respond, decide or react quickly.

teaching.text: Alcohol is a depressant that slows the brain, so responses, decisions and reactions all slow. Remember: depressant slows everything.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alcohol is a depressant that slows the brain, so you cannot respond, decide or react quickly.

question.text: How does alcohol affect judgment of speed, distance and risk?

answer.text: Alcohol weakens your judgment of speed and of distance to other cars, people or objects, and gives false confidence that leads to bigger risks.

teaching.text: Alcohol weakens judgment of speed and distance and breeds false confidence. Remember: false confidence, bad judgment.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alcohol weakens your judgment of speed and of distance to other cars, people or objects, and gives false confidence that leads to bigger risks.

question.text: How does alcohol affect handling several driving tasks at once?

answer.text: Alcohol makes it hard to handle more than one task, so while steering you may miss traffic lights, cars from side streets or pedestrians; it also upsets balance and causes sleepiness.

teaching.text: Alcohol makes juggling tasks hard, so a drinker may miss lights, side-street cars or pedestrians. Remember: one task at a time.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alcohol makes it hard to handle more than one task, so while steering you may miss traffic lights, cars from side streets or pedestrians; it also upsets balance and causes sleepiness.

question.text: What is the only thing that sobers a drinker?

answer.text: Only time sobers a drinker; coffee, a large meal or a cold shower will not.

teaching.text: Nothing but time sobers a drinker, not coffee, a big meal or a cold shower. Remember: only time sobers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Only time sobers a drinker; coffee, a large meal or a cold shower will not.

question.text: Can coffee, a big meal or a cold shower sober up a drinker?

answer.text: Coffee, a big meal and a cold shower do nothing to sober a drinker; only the passing of time does.

teaching.text: Coffee, food and cold showers are myths; only time removes alcohol. Remember: coffee does not sober.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Coffee, a big meal and a cold shower do nothing to sober a drinker; only the passing of time does.

question.text: What are some ways to avoid drinking and driving?

answer.text: Ways to avoid drinking and driving include planning a ride in advance, sharing a taxi, taking public transit, staying overnight with a friend, or riding with someone who has not been drinking.

teaching.text: Plan a ride ahead, share a taxi, take transit, stay over, or ride with someone sober. Remember: plan the ride ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Ways to avoid drinking and driving include planning a ride in advance, sharing a taxi, taking public transit, staying overnight with a friend, or riding with someone who has not been drinking.

question.text: Over a lifetime of driving, what are the rough odds of a serious crash injury or death?

answer.text: Across a typical lifetime behind the wheel, the odds of a serious injury or death in a crash are roughly one in three.

teaching.text: Over a lifetime of driving, the odds of a serious crash injury or death are about one in three. Remember: about one in three.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Across a typical lifetime behind the wheel, the odds of a serious injury or death in a crash are roughly one in three.

question.text: Who must wear a seat belt when a vehicle moves forward on a North Carolina road?

answer.text: In a vehicle built with seat belts, the driver and every passenger must wear a properly fastened belt whenever the vehicle moves forward on a North Carolina street or highway.

teaching.text: In a vehicle built with belts, the driver and every passenger buckle up whenever it moves forward. Remember: everyone buckles, every trip.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a vehicle built with seat belts, the driver and every passenger must wear a properly fastened belt whenever the vehicle moves forward on a North Carolina street or highway.

question.text: Do air bags or automatic shoulder harnesses replace the need for a lap belt?

answer.text: Seat belts are still required in vehicles with air bags, and if the vehicle has automatic shoulder harnesses the lap belt must also be worn.

teaching.text: Air bags never replace belts, and with an automatic shoulder harness the lap belt is still required. Remember: air bags plus belts.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Seat belts are still required in vehicles with air bags, and if the vehicle has automatic shoulder harnesses the lap belt must also be worn.

question.text: If a vehicle has an automatic shoulder harness, is the lap belt still needed?

answer.text: Air bags never excuse the seat belt, and a vehicle with an automatic shoulder harness still requires the lap belt to be fastened.

teaching.text: Air bags supplement belts, and an automatic harness still needs the lap belt. Remember: harness still needs lap belt.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Air bags never excuse the seat belt, and a vehicle with an automatic shoulder harness still requires the lap belt to be fastened.

question.text: Which medical situation exempts an occupant from the seat belt law?

answer.text: The seat belt law exempts an occupant of a noncommercial vehicle whose medical or physical condition, or professionally certified phobia, prevents proper restraint.

teaching.text: A noncommercial occupant whose medical condition or certified phobia prevents restraint is exempt. Remember: certified condition exempts.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The seat belt law exempts an occupant of a noncommercial vehicle whose medical or physical condition, or professionally certified phobia, prevents proper restraint.

question.text: Which on-duty carriers are exempt from the seat belt law?

answer.text: Rural letter carriers of the Postal Service on duty and newspaper carriers delivering along their route are exempt from the seat belt law.

teaching.text: On-duty rural letter carriers and newspaper carriers on their route are exempt. Remember: mail and newspaper carriers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Rural letter carriers of the Postal Service on duty and newspaper carriers delivering along their route are exempt from the seat belt law.

question.text: When are frequent-stop delivery occupants exempt from wearing belts?

answer.text: Drivers or passengers who keep stopping to leave the vehicle or deliver items are exempt if the vehicle goes no faster than twenty miles per hour between stops.

teaching.text: Frequent-stop delivery occupants are exempt only at twenty miles per hour or less between stops. Remember: slow deliveries exempt.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers or passengers who keep stopping to leave the vehicle or deliver items are exempt if the vehicle goes no faster than twenty miles per hour between stops.

question.text: What speed limit keeps the frequent-delivery belt exemption valid?

answer.text: The frequent-delivery seat belt exemption applies only if the vehicle stays at or below twenty miles per hour between stops.

teaching.text: Going faster than twenty miles per hour between stops ends the delivery exemption. Remember: twenty or slower between stops.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The frequent-delivery seat belt exemption applies only if the vehicle stays at or below twenty miles per hour between stops.

question.text: Which farm, equipment and seating situations are exempt from the seat belt law?

answer.text: Other exemptions cover property-carrying vehicles used for farming within the state, vehicles not legally required to have belts, and situations where every belted or restraint-equipped seat is already taken.

teaching.text: Farm property vehicles within the state, vehicles without required belts, and full belted seats are exempt. Remember: farm, no belts, full seats.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Other exemptions cover property-carrying vehicles used for farming within the state, vehicles not legally required to have belts, and situations where every belted or restraint-equipped seat is already taken.

question.text: When are motor home occupants exempt from the seat belt law?

answer.text: In a motor home, occupants other than the driver and front-seat passengers are exempt when the motor home has at least four of the listed living facilities.

teaching.text: Rear motor home occupants are exempt when the motor home has at least four listed living facilities. Remember: motor home rear riders.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a motor home, occupants other than the driver and front-seat passengers are exempt when the motor home has at least four of the listed living facilities.

question.text: How many unrestrained child deaths could correctly used safety seats prevent?

answer.text: Correctly used safety seats could save seven of every ten children who die while riding unrestrained.

teaching.text: Correct safety seat use could save seven of every ten children who die riding unrestrained. Remember: seats save most kids.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Correctly used safety seats could save seven of every ten children who die while riding unrestrained.

question.text: What makes a child safety seat the best choice, and where can families find low-cost seats?

answer.text: The best child seat is one used on every ride that fits your car and has a comfortable harness or shield, and low-cost rentals are often offered by local groups, hospitals and health departments.

teaching.text: The best seat is used every ride, fits your car and is comfortable, and low-cost rentals are often available. Remember: the seat you always use.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The best child seat is one used on every ride that fits your car and has a comfortable harness or shield, and low-cost rentals are often offered by local groups, hospitals and health departments.

question.text: What must a driver do for every passenger under sixteen?

answer.text: A driver carrying any passenger under sixteen must make sure each one is secured in a child restraint or seat belt meeting the federal standards in force when it was made.

teaching.text: The driver makes sure every passenger under sixteen is in a compliant restraint or seat belt. Remember: under sixteen, restrained.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver carrying any passenger under sixteen must make sure each one is secured in a child restraint or seat belt meeting the federal standards in force when it was made.

question.text: What restraint must a child younger than eight and under eighty pounds use?

answer.text: A child younger than eight who weighs under eighty pounds must ride in a weight-appropriate child passenger restraint.

teaching.text: A child under eight and under eighty pounds rides in a weight-appropriate restraint. Remember: under eight and eighty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A child younger than eight who weighs under eighty pounds must ride in a weight-appropriate child passenger restraint.

question.text: When must a young child ride in the rear seat because of a front air bag?

answer.text: When a vehicle has an active front passenger air bag and a rear seat, a child under five weighing under forty pounds must ride in the rear unless the restraint is built for use with a front air bag.

teaching.text: With an active front air bag and a rear seat, a child under five and under forty pounds rides in back unless the restraint is built for it. Remember: small kids behind air bags.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a vehicle has an active front passenger air bag and a rear seat, a child under five weighing under forty pounds must ride in the rear unless the restraint is built for use with a front air bag.

question.text: How do the under-eight rule and the rear-seat air bag rule differ in age and weight?

answer.text: A child under eight and under eighty pounds needs a weight-appropriate restraint, while the rear-seat rule near an active front air bag covers a child under five and under forty pounds.

teaching.text: Eight goes with eighty for the restraint rule, and five goes with forty for the rear-seat rule. Remember: eight-eighty versus five-forty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A child under eight and under eighty pounds needs a weight-appropriate restraint, while the rear-seat rule near an active front air bag covers a child under five and under forty pounds.

question.text: When may a child under eight weighing forty to eighty pounds use a lap belt alone?

answer.text: If no seat has a lap and shoulder belt for the restraint, a child under eight weighing forty to eighty pounds may ride with a properly fitted lap belt alone.

teaching.text: A child under eight at forty to eighty pounds may use a lap belt alone only when no seat has a lap and shoulder belt. Remember: lap only without shoulder belt.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If no seat has a lap and shoulder belt for the restraint, a child under eight weighing forty to eighty pounds may ride with a properly fitted lap belt alone.

question.text: What condition must be true before a lap belt alone is allowed for a young child?

answer.text: A lap belt alone is allowed for a child under eight weighing forty to eighty pounds only when no seat has a lap and shoulder belt for the restraint.

teaching.text: The lap-belt-only exception needs every seat to lack a lap and shoulder belt for the restraint. Remember: no shoulder belt available.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A lap belt alone is allowed for a child under eight weighing forty to eighty pounds only when no seat has a lap and shoulder belt for the restraint.

question.text: How long should a child use a booster seat, and how should the adult belt fit?

answer.text: Children who have outgrown safety seats should use federally compliant booster seats until an adult belt fits: lap belt snug on the hips, not the stomach, and shoulder belt across the shoulder and chest, not the face or throat.

teaching.text: Use a compliant booster until the lap belt sits on the hips and the shoulder belt crosses the chest. Remember: booster until the belt fits.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Children who have outgrown safety seats should use federally compliant booster seats until an adult belt fits: lap belt snug on the hips, not the stomach, and shoulder belt across the shoulder and chest, not the face or throat.

question.text: How fast does an air bag deploy?

answer.text: An air bag bursts out of the dashboard at up to two hundred miles per hour, faster than an eye blink, so it is far from a soft pillow.

teaching.text: An air bag explodes outward at up to two hundred miles per hour, so it is no soft pillow. Remember: air bags hit hard.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An air bag bursts out of the dashboard at up to two hundred miles per hour, faster than an eye blink, so it is far from a soft pillow.

question.text: Where should children twelve and younger ride?

answer.text: Children aged twelve and younger should ride buckled up in a rear seat.

teaching.text: Children twelve and younger should ride buckled in a rear seat. Remember: twelve and under in back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Children aged twelve and younger should ride buckled up in a rear seat.

question.text: Where must a rear-facing infant never ride?

answer.text: An infant in a rear-facing safety seat must never ride in the front seat of a vehicle that has a passenger-side air bag.

teaching.text: Never put a rear-facing infant seat in front of a passenger-side air bag. Remember: rear-facing never in front.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An infant in a rear-facing safety seat must never ride in the front seat of a vehicle that has a passenger-side air bag.

question.text: How should the lap and shoulder belts be positioned with air bags?

answer.text: Air bags only supplement belts: wear the lap belt under the abdomen and low on the hips, and the shoulder belt over the collarbone, away from the neck and across the breastbone.

teaching.text: Wear the lap belt low on the hips and the shoulder belt over the collarbone and across the breastbone. Remember: low lap, chest shoulder.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Air bags only supplement belts: wear the lap belt under the abdomen and low on the hips, and the shoulder belt over the collarbone, away from the neck and across the breastbone.

question.text: How far forward should the driver and front passenger seats be?

answer.text: Move the driver and front passenger seats as far back as practical, especially for shorter people.

teaching.text: Slide the front seats as far back as practical, especially for shorter people. Remember: seats back, especially short people.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Move the driver and front passenger seats as far back as practical, especially for shorter people.

question.text: What helmet must motorcycle and moped riders and passengers wear?

answer.text: Every motorcycle or moped operator and passenger must wear a safety helmet meeting Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard two hundred eighteen.

teaching.text: Every motorcycle and moped operator and passenger wears a helmet meeting the federal safety standard. Remember: helmet meeting federal standard.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every motorcycle or moped operator and passenger must wear a safety helmet meeting Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard two hundred eighteen.

question.text: What marks a compliant motorcycle helmet?

answer.text: A compliant helmet has a firm polystyrene liner about one inch thick and a DOT symbol fixed permanently on the back by the maker; a sticker added later does not make it legal.

teaching.text: A compliant helmet has a firm liner about an inch thick and the maker's permanent DOT symbol. Remember: maker's DOT, firm liner.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A compliant helmet has a firm polystyrene liner about one inch thick and a DOT symbol fixed permanently on the back by the maker; a sticker added later does not make it legal.

question.text: Does adding a DOT sticker make a helmet compliant?

answer.text: A DOT symbol fixed permanently by the manufacturer marks a compliant helmet, while a DOT sticker sold separately or added by the rider does not.

teaching.text: Only the manufacturer's permanent DOT symbol counts; an added sticker does not. Remember: sticker is not compliance.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A DOT symbol fixed permanently by the manufacturer marks a compliant helmet, while a DOT sticker sold separately or added by the rider does not.

question.text: Who may not ride in the open bed of a pickup truck, and who is responsible?

answer.text: North Carolina bars children younger than sixteen from riding in the open bed of a pickup truck, and the driver is responsible for compliance, though the statute has some exemptions.

teaching.text: Children under sixteen may not ride in an open pickup bed, and the driver is responsible. Remember: no kids in pickup beds.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: North Carolina bars children younger than sixteen from riding in the open bed of a pickup truck, and the driver is responsible for compliance, though the statute has some exemptions.

question.text: How does the rear-seat age advice compare with the pickup bed law?

answer.text: Riding in the rear seat is advised for children twelve and under, while riding in an open pickup bed is prohibited by law for children under sixteen.

teaching.text: The rear-seat guidance for twelve and under is advice, while the under-sixteen pickup bed ban is law. Remember: twelve advised, sixteen required.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Riding in the rear seat is advised for children twelve and under, while riding in an open pickup bed is prohibited by law for children under sixteen.
